title: CSV vs Excel vs JSON: Differences and When to Use Each
desc: CSV, Excel (XLSX) and JSON compared: structure, data types, formulas, size limits and encoding, which to use for what, and how to convert between them for free.
h1s: CSV vs Excel vs JSON: the differences and when to use each
headings: CSV vs Excel vs JSON: the differences and when to use each
text: HomeGuidesCSV vs Excel vs JSONCSV vs Excel vs JSON: the differences and when to use eachWhat each format can hold, where each one breaks, and a simple rule for picking the right one.By OpenAnyDoc · Published October 30, 2026The short answerUse CSV for one table of plain data that many programs must read, Excel (.xlsx) for workbooks people open and edit with formulas and formatting, and JSON for structured or nested data that programs read and write.CSV: one plain tableA CSV file is plain text: one line per row, with values separated by commas, or by semicolons in many countries. It has no types, sheets, formulas or formatting, so every program can read it and files stay small. The cost is ambiguity: neither the separator nor the text encoding is stored in the file, which is why CSV files sometimes open in one column or show broken Arabic in Excel.Excel (.xlsx): a workbookAn .xlsx file is a zip archive of XML files in the Office Open XML format. It holds several sheets, typed cells (numbers, dates, text), formulas, number formats, styles, charts and more. A sheet holds at most 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns. It is the right format when people will open the file, but it is harder for scripts to write and read than CSV.JSON: structured dataJSON is text too, but it stores objects and lists that can nest: an order can contain a customer and a list of items. Values are typed as strings, numbers, true or false, and null; there is no date type, so dates are written as text. Almost every programming language reads it, which is why APIs use it, but a spreadsheet cannot show the nesting without flattening it.Side by sideThe differences that matter in practice:Structure: CSV is one table; Excel has several sheets; JSON has nested objects and lists.Types: CSV has none, everything is text; Excel has numbers, dates, text and true/false; JSON has strings, numbers, true/false and null.Formulas and formatting: only Excel.Size: the CSV and JSON formats have no limit; Excel stops at about a million rows per sheet.Who reads it: CSV, almost everything; Excel, spreadsheet apps and libraries; JSON, programs, APIs and dedicated viewers.Text encoding: not recorded in a CSV file; Excel and JSON handle Unicode by design, and JSON exchanged between systems must be UTF-8.Which one to pickA rule of thumb for the common cases:Sending a table to someone who will open it in Excel: .xlsx, so nothing about separators or encoding can go wrong.Importing into a database or another program: CSV in UTF-8.Data for an app, an API or a configuration file: JSON.Data with more than about a million rows: CSV or JSON, because Excel cannot hold it in one sheet.Converting between themEach conversion runs in your browser, uploads nothing, and opens the result in its own viewer: Excel to CSV, CSV to Excel, Excel to JSON, CSV to JSON and JSON to CSV. Turning JSON into a table flattens nested fields into columns such as address.city, and converting a CSV makes its header row the JSON keys.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com if a conversion does not give you what you expected (no personal data).

text: HomeGuidesFill a PDF form without AcrobatHow to fill in a PDF form without AcrobatHow to tell a fillable form from a flat one, how to fill in each kind on a computer or phone, and how to flatten and sign it before you send it.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerYou do not need Adobe Acrobat to fill in a PDF form. If the form has fillable fields, browsers, Preview on a Mac and the Files app on an iPhone can fill them, and OpenAnyDoc's Fill PDF form does it in your browser without uploading the file, then can flatten the answers so they cannot be changed. If the form is a flat page with no fields, type your answers on it with text boxes in Edit PDF.First, find out what kind of form you havePDF forms come in three kinds, and the way to fill one depends on which it is:A fillable form has real fields; the standard kind is called AcroForm. Click a line and a cursor appears, or click a box and it shows a tick. The answers are stored in the fields, so they can be read and changed later.A flat form only looks like a form: a scan, or a page saved without fields. Clicking does nothing, so you place text where each answer goes.An XFA form was made with Adobe LiveCycle, an older Adobe format still used by some organisations. Outside Adobe's apps it often shows only a message instead of the form. Fill PDF form does not support XFA, and such forms usually need Adobe Acrobat Reader, which is free.Fill in a fillable form, with nothing uploadedFill PDF form works on any computer or phone with a modern browser:Open Fill PDF form and choose your PDF, or drop it on the page. If the PDF has no fields, the tool says so and points you to Edit PDF.Click each field and type, tick or choose your answer. Text fields, multi-line boxes, checkboxes, radio buttons and drop-down lists all work, in English, Arabic or any language your keyboard types.Tick Flatten on save if the answers should be fixed, then click Save a copy and download the filled form.Your form stays on your deviceForms often hold names, addresses and ID numbers, so it matters where they go. The form is filled by your own browser and never sent to a server, and you can check that nothing is uploaded with your browser's network panel. The original file is not changed: Save a copy makes a new PDF.On a phoneOpen Fill PDF form in your phone's browser, choose the file from your downloads or the Files app and tap each field. The phone's own apps can fill many forms too:iPhone and iPad: open the PDF in the Files app and tap a field to type in it. On a form without fields, the Markup button adds text and a signature.Android: the Google Drive app opens PDFs and can fill in many fillable forms.A flat form: type where the answers goWhen a form has no fields, use Edit PDF. Choose Text box, click where an answer goes and type it, then drag the box into line. Tick a box by typing an X in it, or draw a tick with the Draw tool. Click Save a copy when every answer is in place.If you send the same form to many people, PDF Forms turns the flat page into a fillable one. Place text boxes, checkboxes, drop-down lists, choice buttons, date fields and a signature box, and the saved copy can be filled in Acrobat, Preview, browsers and Fill PDF form. Drop-down choices and starting values take Latin letters for now, but people can type Arabic into the fields.Flatten before you send itA filled form keeps its answers in fields, so anyone who opens it can change them. Flatten on save draws every answer onto the page and removes the fields, so the copy you send stays as you filled it. Leave it off when someone else still has to fill in part of the form.Flattened answers are drawn as pictures, so they cannot be selected or searched afterwards.Sign itMany forms end with a signature. Fill in the fields first, then open the saved copy in Sign PDF: the next steps after the download pass it on without choosing the file again. Draw your signature with a mouse or finger, type your name in a signature style, or upload a picture of it, and place it on the line. This is a visual signature, like signing a printout, not a certificate-based digital signature. The guide to signing a PDF without Adobe explains the difference and the free options on every device.Other free ways on a computerYou may not need a website at all:Chrome, Edge and Firefox fill in the fields of most fillable forms in a browser tab and save a copy with your answers.Preview on a Mac fills in fields, and on a flat form adds text boxes and signatures from its Markup toolbar.Adobe Acrobat Reader is free as well, and is the safe choice for XFA forms.If the form will not openA form that asks for a password, or that no app will open, has a different problem from filling it in. The guide on how to open a PDF without Adobe lists the usual causes and what to do about each.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe the form you are trying to fill in (no personal data).

title: Why Your CSV Shows Broken Arabic in Excel (and the Fix)
desc: Arabic in a CSV turns into Ø§Ù„ symbols or question marks in Excel because the file has no UTF-8 marker. Three fixes, one of them free with no upload at all.
h1s: Why your CSV shows broken Arabic text in Excel
headings: Why your CSV shows broken Arabic text in Excel
What the broken text looks like
Why Excel gets the encoding wrong
Fix 1: download an Excel-ready copy (free, nothing uploaded)
Fix 2: import the file instead of opening it
Fix 3: write the file the right way next time
The reverse case: a file that only Excel reads correctly
When the letters are right but the order is wrong
text: HomeGuidesFix broken Arabic in a CSVWhy your CSV shows broken Arabic text in ExcelExcel guesses the wrong encoding when a UTF-8 file has no byte order mark. Here is what happens, and three ways to fix it.By OpenAnyDoc · Published October 20, 2026What the broken text looks likeYou export a report, open the CSV in Excel, and the Arabic column reads "Ø§Ù„Ø±ÙŠØ§Ø¶" instead of "الرياض". Sometimes it is a row of question marks or empty boxes instead. The data in the file is almost always intact; Excel has only read it with the wrong character encoding.Why Excel gets the encoding wrongA CSV file is plain text, and plain text carries no label saying which encoding it uses. Nearly every system today writes UTF-8, which covers Arabic and every other script.When you double-click a .csv, Excel does not ask. It assumes the old Windows code page of your computer (Windows-1252 on an English PC, Windows-1256 on an Arabic one) unless the file starts with a three-byte UTF-8 marker called the byte order mark, or BOM. Most exports leave the BOM out, so Excel reads each Arabic letter as two or three Latin symbols. Tab-separated files (.tsv) have exactly the same problem.Fix 1: download an Excel-ready copy (free, nothing uploaded)OpenAnyDoc adds the missing marker for you, and the file never leaves your computer:Open the CSV viewer and drop the file on the page. It checks for a BOM, UTF-16 and UTF-8, and falls back to Windows-1256 for older Arabic files; the status bar at the bottom shows the encoding it found.If the file has Arabic text and no BOM, an "Excel copy" button appears in the status bar. Click it.A copy named like your file with "-excel" added is downloaded, with the UTF-8 marker and Windows line endings. Double-click that copy and Excel shows the Arabic correctly.Fix 2: import the file instead of opening itExcel reads the encoding correctly when you import rather than double-click: go to Data, then Get Data, From File, From Text/CSV (older versions: Data, From Text), pick the file, set File Origin to "65001: Unicode (UTF-8)" and load it. It works every time, but you have to repeat it for every file, and the result is a workbook rather than the CSV itself.The normal Download button in OpenAnyDoc also adds the marker whenever the file holds non-English text, so any copy you edit there opens cleanly in Excel too. If Excel refuses the file altogether because it has more than about a million rows, the large CSV viewer opens it in the browser instead.Fix 3: write the file the right way next timeIf the CSV is made in Excel, use Save As and choose "CSV UTF-8 (Comma delimited)": that format writes the BOM. If it comes from code or an export tool, write UTF-8 with a BOM for files that will be opened in Excel, or export an .xlsx workbook instead, which stores its encoding and never has this problem. You can check an XLSX in the Excel viewer without opening Excel.The reverse case: a file that only Excel reads correctlyExports from older Arabic systems are often Windows-1256 with no UTF-8 at all. Excel on an Arabic PC shows them fine, while browsers, editors and most modern tools assume UTF-8 and show nonsense. OpenAnyDoc reads such a file as Windows-1256 automatically, and if the guess is wrong you can pick the encoding yourself in the status bar. Downloading then writes UTF-8 with the marker, so the file opens correctly everywhere.When the letters are right but the order is wrongIf the Arabic letters themselves are correct but numbers, brackets or English words sit on the wrong side, the encoding is fine. That is text direction: set the cell or sheet to right-to-left in Excel (Page Layout, then Sheet Right-to-Left, or the paragraph direction buttons). In OpenAnyDoc, cells with Arabic text are shown right-to-left automatically.Still broken?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe what you see. Do not send the file if it holds personal data; the first line is usually enough.

headings: Why Arabic text copied from a PDF comes out reversed, and how to fix it

text: HomeGuidesArabic text from a PDF reversedWhy Arabic text copied from a PDF comes out reversed, and how to fix itWhat a PDF stores instead of sentences, why Arabic copies backwards, and how to get the text out in reading order without uploading the file.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerArabic text comes out reversed or broken because a PDF does not store sentences. It stores the shape of each letter and its place on the page, and many PDF readers copy those shapes in the order they sit on the page, from left to right, so the words come out backwards or with separated letters. Open the file in OpenAnyDoc's PDF viewer, or save its text with PDF to text or PDF to Word: they rebuild Arabic lines in reading order before you copy them.Why it happensA Word document or a web page keeps text as it was typed: the letters in typing order, and the program shapes and orders them for the screen. A PDF is closer to a printout. It keeps the drawn shapes of the letters with the place on the page where each one goes, plus only as much information about the text behind them as the program that made the PDF chose to write.The page still looks right, because each shape is drawn where it belongs; the trouble shows only when the text is taken out, and each reader turns the shapes back into text in its own way. For Arabic, three things can go wrong:Letters stored in visual order. Some programs place every Arabic letter on its own, left to right as it appears on the page. A reader that copies them in that order gives you each word backwards and the words of the line in reverse.Joined shapes instead of letters. Arabic letters change shape at the start, middle and end of a word. Some PDFs record those shapes, called presentation forms, instead of the ordinary letters, so pasted text can look right yet not match when you search for it, or show letters that do not join.Mixed lines. A number, a date or an English word inside an Arabic sentence runs left to right, and brackets face the other way in right-to-left text. A reader that ignores direction moves them to the wrong place or flips the brackets.Copy Arabic in reading order, with nothing uploadedOpenAnyDoc's PDF tools rebuild right-to-left lines before you see the text. When a line is mostly Arabic, its pieces are put back in reading order from right to left, an English word or a number inside it keeps its own order, brackets are turned back into the character that was typed, and joined shapes become ordinary Arabic letters. Pick the tool that matches what you need:A few lines: open the file in the PDF viewer, select the text and copy it. Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on a Mac) searches the Arabic text and highlights the matches.All of the text: PDF to text saves every page as a .txt file, Arabic in reading order, with optional markers where each page starts.Text you want to edit: PDF to Word writes an editable .docx with Arabic paragraphs set right to left, keeping headings, lists and pictures.Private files stay on your deviceThe PDF is read by your own browser and never uploaded, so this works for contracts, statements and other documents you would not send to a website. You can check that nothing is uploaded in your browser's network panel. Once the page has loaded, the viewer and PDF to text keep working without an internet connection.Nothing to select? The PDF is a scanA scanned PDF, or one made from phone photos, holds a picture of each page and no text at all. Nothing can be selected, search finds nothing, and PDF to text tells you it found no text. Run OCR PDF first: it reads the words on each page, in Arabic, English or both, and lays them over the page as invisible text, so the page looks exactly as before. Then copy from the new file in the viewer, or open it in PDF to text or PDF to Word.Text recognition makes mistakes, more so on blurry, small or handwritten text, so check names, numbers and dates against the page before you rely on them.Check the result yourselfA one-minute test tells you whether a copy is right:Pick a line and note its first word, the one at its right edge. Copy the line and paste it into a note or an email.The first word should be at the start of the pasted line (on the right in a right-to-left editor), and the letters of each word should join as they do on the page.If the last word comes first, or the letters stand apart, the copy is reversed or broken: copy it again from the PDF viewer here.Search the PDF for an Arabic word you can see on the page. If the viewer finds and highlights it, the text inside the file is usable.What it cannot fixSome limits are worth knowing before you start:Tables come out as lines of text, not as a table. PDF to Word keeps the columns of a line apart with tab stops; PDF to Excel reads tables into cells.A PDF that needs a password to open must be unlocked first; Unlock PDF removes the password when you know it.If a PDF's letters copy as symbols in every reader, the file has no usable text behind them. Treat it like a scan: OCR PDF leaves pages that already have text as they are unless you choose otherwise, so choose to read those pages too.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe how the copied text looks (no personal data).

title: How Many Tokens Is My PDF? Count It Before You Paste
desc: What a token is, why Arabic, tables and the AI model change the count, why pages are a poor guide, and how to count a PDF's tokens in your browser, no upload.
h1s: How many tokens is my PDF?
headings: How many tokens is my PDF?
Why a page count is a poor guide
How to count your own PDF exactly
If the number is too high
text: HomeGuidesTokens in a PDFHow many tokens is my PDF?What decides a PDF's token count, measured examples in English, Arabic and a table, and how to count your own file exactly.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerThere is no fixed number of tokens per page: it depends on how many words the page holds, the language they are in, whether it is mostly tables, and which AI model reads it. In our test, a page of 415 English words came to 467 tokens, the same text in Arabic to 571, and a page holding one table of 40 rows to 889. To know your own file's number, drop it into OpenAnyDoc's Token counter, which counts it in your browser without uploading it.What a token isAn AI model does not read letters or words. It reads tokens: pieces of text that it treats as one unit. A short common word is often one token, a long or rare word is split into several, and punctuation, numbers and spaces take tokens too.Counting words is not the same thing. On our English test page below, 415 words came to 467 tokens, a little over one token per word, but that ratio changes from file to file.Chat limits, file limits and the prices of AI services are counted in tokens. A long conversation also counts everything said before and the answer being written, so a document that only just fits may leave little room for the reply.Why a page count is a poor guide"Ten pages" can mean very different amounts of text. We measured three synthetic pages with the same counter the site uses:A report page of plain English prose, 415 words: 467 tokens.The same report written in Arabic, 319 words: 571 tokens, about a fifth more for the same meaning.A page with one table of 40 rows and 5 columns (codes, regions, prices, totals), 247 words: 889 tokens, nearly twice the prose page with fewer words.A scanned page: 0 tokens until text recognition adds its text, because the page is only a picture.Where the differences come fromTables cost more because numbers, codes and the | marks between cells are short pieces that are rarely joined into one token. Font size, margins and pictures change how many words fit on a page at all.Language matters because tokenizers learn their pieces from text, and most of that text is English. English words are often a single token; Arabic words, with their attached prefixes and suffixes, are more often split. That is why the Arabic page above had fewer words but more tokens.Why the model mattersEvery AI model has its own tokenizer, so the same PDF gives a different number in each. OpenAnyDoc counts with one standard tokenizer that some widely used models share. For other models, Claude and Gemini among them, the number is an estimate, usually close but not exact. When a file is near a limit, leave some room rather than relying on the last few hundred tokens.How to count your own PDF exactlyToken counter reads the file on your device; nothing is sent to a server or to an AI service:Open Token counter and choose your PDF, or drop it on the page. Word, PowerPoint, Excel, CSV, JSON, TXT and Markdown files work too, or you can paste text.The PDF is turned into the same Markdown that PDF to Markdown makes, so you count the text you would actually paste.Read the tokens, words and characters under the text box.The text box can be edited: delete the parts you will not paste and the count updates.If the number is too highSend less rather than hoping the chat copes:Keep only the pages you need with Extract PDF pages, then count again.Cut a long report into parts with Split PDF and paste one part at a time, telling the chat to wait until the last part arrives.For lists of records in JSON, JSON to TOON writes the same data in a shorter form.If the count is 0, the PDF is scanned; run OCR PDF first.Tables cost the most, so paste them in a form the chat can read. Giving ChatGPT a PDF without losing the tables shows how.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe the file and the count you see (no personal data).

desc: Merge PDF files on any device: Preview on a Mac, Files or Shortcuts on iPhone, the browser on Windows and Android, plus page order, photos and file size.
h1s: How to merge PDF files on any device
headings: How to merge PDF files on any device
On an iPhone or iPad: Files or Shortcuts
In your browser, with nothing uploaded
If a file will not merge
text: HomeGuidesMerge PDF files on any deviceHow to merge PDF files on any deviceThe free ways to combine PDFs on a computer or phone, which of them need no install, and how to handle order, photos, blank pages and size.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026 · Updated November 23, 2026The short answerA Mac can merge PDFs with Preview, and an iPhone or iPad with the Files app or a shortcut. Windows and Android have no merge built in, so the simplest way there is a browser tool. OpenAnyDoc's Merge PDF works in any modern browser on any of these devices and joins the files on your device, without uploading them.On a Mac: PreviewPreview, the PDF app that comes with every Mac, can add one PDF to another. Open the first PDF, choose View, then Thumbnails, and select the page after which the next file should go. Choose Edit, then Insert, then Page from File, and pick the other PDF. Drag thumbnails to change the order. Preview changes the file you opened, so if you want to keep the original, make a copy first with File, then Duplicate, and save the copy.On Windows: no built-in mergeWindows opens and prints PDFs in Microsoft Edge, but neither Edge nor Windows has a command that joins two PDFs. Printing to Microsoft Print to PDF makes a new PDF from one file at a time, so it cannot combine files either. You can install a PDF program, or use a tool in the browser you already have: open Merge PDF in Edge or Chrome, and there is nothing to install and nothing uploaded.On an iPhone or iPad: Files or ShortcutsIn the Files app, open the folder that holds the PDFs, tap Select, tap each file, then tap the More button (three dots) and choose Create PDF. A new PDF appears in the same folder. Files decides the order of the pages, so open the result and check it; if it is wrong, use a browser tool where you set the order yourself.The Shortcuts app has a Make PDF action that joins whatever it is given into one PDF. A shortcut that takes files from the share sheet and passes them to Make PDF is handy if you merge files often.On Android: use the browserAndroid has no merge built in, and the file apps that phone makers add differ. Open Merge PDF in Chrome or another browser, tap Choose a file and pick the PDFs from your downloads or another folder. On a phone, set the order with the arrows under each file.In your browser, with nothing uploadedMerge PDF works the same on a computer or phone:Choose two or more PDFs, or drop them on the page. You can add more at any time.Drag the thumbnails into order, or use the arrows under each file.Click Merge PDF and download one file, named after the first PDF.Getting the order rightMerge PDF orders whole files: each thumbnail is a file's first page, and all its pages follow in their own order. That covers most jobs, such as a cover letter, then a form, then three receipts.If single pages need to move, for example to put one page of the second file in the middle of the first, merge first and then pass the result to Organize PDF. The next steps after the download hand the file over without choosing it again. Organize PDF also turns, duplicates and deletes pages, and Remove PDF pages drops pages you do not want to send.Adding photos or blank pagesMerge PDF takes PDF files only. To add a photo of a receipt or a screenshot, turn it into a PDF first with JPG to PDF, then merge it with the rest. The guide on turning photos into one PDF covers page size and margins.To add a blank page, open the merged file in Organize PDF and insert one: it takes the size of the page before it. This is useful before printing on both sides, so that each document starts on a new sheet.File sizeMerging copies the pages as they are, so text stays sharp and selectable, and the merged file is about as large as the files added together. Merging does not make anything smaller; to shrink the merged file afterwards, open it in Compress PDF.If the files are large because they are full of camera photos, make the photos smaller with Compress image before you turn them into a PDF. If the merged file is too big to email, cut it into parts again with Split PDF; the guide on how to split a PDF explains the page ranges. Very large sets of files are limited by your device's memory.If a file will not mergeThree things can get in the way:A PDF that needs a password to open cannot be read. If you know the password, remove it first with Unlock PDF, which also runs in your browser.Bookmarks and fillable form fields of the original files may not carry over. Fill in a form first with Fill PDF form and tick Flatten on save, so the answers stay as part of the page.A file that no app will open may be damaged; Repair PDF tries to rebuild it.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe the files you are trying to merge (no personal data).

title: How to Split a PDF: Separate Pages or Save Only Some
desc: Split a PDF into separate files by page ranges, every few pages or one per page, or save only the pages you need, in the browser or with Preview and Edge.
h1s: How to split a PDF or save only some pages
headings: How to split a PDF or save only some pages
One file per page, in a ZIP
text: HomeGuidesSplit a PDFHow to split a PDF or save only some pagesWhich tool fits which job, how to write page ranges, one file per page in a ZIP, and the free ways already on your computer.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerFirst decide what you want back: several files from one PDF, or one file with only some of its pages. Split PDF does the first, by page ranges, every few pages, or one file per page in a ZIP; Extract PDF pages saves the pages you click as one new PDF, and Remove PDF pages saves the PDF without the ones you click. All three run in your browser, nothing is uploaded, and your original file stays as it was.Which tool for which jobPick by the result you need:Several files, each with its own pages: Split PDF, by page ranges or every few pages.Every page as its own file: Split PDF with One file per page, or Extract PDF pages with One PDF per page.One file with a few chosen pages: Extract PDF pages.The same file minus a few pages: Remove PDF pages.The same pages in a new order: Organize PDF.How to write page rangesIn Split PDF, choose By page ranges and type the ranges separated by commas. A hyphen means "from this page to that one", and each range becomes its own PDF. Page numbers count from the first page of the file, not from the numbers printed on the pages.Say a 12-page report has a two-page summary, eight pages of findings and a two-page appendix. Typing 1-2, 3-10, 11-12 gives three PDFs, one for each part. Typing 5 alone gives a file with page 5. Arabic digits and the Arabic comma work too.If the file is a stack of same-length documents, such as 30 pages of three-page forms, choose Every few pages and set 3 to get ten files. Several files come in one ZIP, named after your PDF and its page numbers.One file per page, in a ZIPChoose One file per page and every page becomes its own PDF, all in one ZIP. Most computers and phones open a ZIP when you double-click or tap it, and show the PDFs inside. This is the way to send page 4 to one person and page 7 to another, or to hand pages to a system that takes one document per upload.Saving only some pagesWhen you want one smaller PDF rather than many, use Extract PDF pages: click the thumbnails you want, Shift+click to pick a run, and download them as a new PDF. The pages keep the order they have in the original, and the name tells you what is inside, such as report-pages-2,4-6.pdf.When only a few pages must go, Remove PDF pages is quicker: click the ones to delete and download the rest. A PDF needs at least one page, so it will not remove them all. If the kept pages also need a new order, pass the result to Organize PDF.Without a websiteA computer can also save some pages as a new PDF through its print dialog:Mac: open the PDF in Preview, choose File, then Print, type the pages you want, then choose Save as PDF from the PDF menu. You can also drag a page thumbnail from Preview's sidebar to the desktop to get that page on its own.Windows: open the PDF in Microsoft Edge, choose Print, pick Microsoft Print to PDF as the printer, type the pages, and print to a new file.Android: the print dialog has a Save as PDF printer and lets you choose pages.What carries overSplit PDF copies pages as they are, so text stays sharp and selectable, and pictures keep their quality. A 150-page PDF splits in seconds, with a progress bar. Printing to PDF, as above, makes the pages again through the print system, so links and form fields may be lost; the tools here copy them instead.Bookmarks and links that jump between pages may not carry over to the new files. A PDF that needs a password to open must have the password removed first with Unlock PDF, if you know it.After splittingEach part is an ordinary PDF. You can join parts with other files again, as the guide on how to merge PDF files shows, number each part's pages from 1 with Add page numbers, or put a password on a part before you send it, as explained in password-protecting a PDF.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe how you want the PDF split (no personal data).

mainEntity.name: Is it safe to open my files online? Are they uploaded?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your files are not uploaded. Your browser reads the file and shows it on your screen, so it never leaves your device and there is nothing for us to store, see or lose.

mainEntity.name: Which file types can I open?

Excel files keep formulas, number formats and merged cells; charts, images and macros are not kept.

mainEntity.name: How big can a file be?

mainEntity.name: Why getters and setters instead of public fields?

mainEntity.name: Why long and not int?

acceptedAnswer.text: Not on its own, because the fields are camelCase and carry no annotations. Set a naming strategy, such as PropertyNamingStrategies.SNAKE_CASE on your ObjectMapper, or add @JsonProperty("order_id") to the fields that differ.

mainEntity.name: The code is one file. Will it compile?

acceptedAnswer.text: Java allows only one public top-level class per file. Move each public class into a file named after it, or make the others package-private, and it compiles.

title: JSON Unexpected Token Error: Find the Line and Fix It
desc: Unexpected token in JSON means the parser hit something the format forbids: a trailing comma, a quote, HTML. What each token means, where to look, and the fix.
h1s: JSON "unexpected token" errors: find the line and fix it
headings: JSON "unexpected token" errors: find the line and fix it
Fix it automatically when it is one of the usual mistakes
A byte order mark at position 0
text: HomeGuidesJSON unexpected tokenJSON "unexpected token" errors: find the line and fix itThe parser stopped at a character JSON does not allow. Here is what each token means, how to find the exact line, and how to fix it.By OpenAnyDoc · Published October 22, 2026What the error means"Unexpected token } in JSON at position 412", "Unexpected end of JSON input", "Unexpected token < in JSON at position 0": every one of these comes from a JSON parser that read something the format does not allow. JSON is strict. One stray comma, a comment, or a single quote is enough, and the parser stops at the first character it cannot accept, which is often one character after the real mistake.The five usual causesRead the token in the message; it tells you which one you have:Unexpected token < at position 0: the text is an HTML page, not JSON. A server answered with an error or login page. Open the address in the browser and look at what it really returns.Unexpected token u at position 0: the text is the word undefined. A variable was empty before it was parsed.Unexpected end of JSON input: the text stops early, usually an empty response or a file cut off while saving.Unexpected token } or ]: a trailing comma before a closing bracket ({"a": 1,}), which JavaScript allows and JSON does not.Unexpected token ' or a letter: single quotes, unquoted keys ({name: "x"}), a comment (// or /* */), or the words True, None, NaN or Infinity, which come from Python and are not JSON.Find the exact spotThe position in the message counts characters from the start, which is useless in a long file. The JSON validator shows the same parser message with the line and column, and Go to error selects that place in the text. Paste the text or drop the .json file; a file with a syntax error opens too, and the error shows right away. Nothing is uploaded: the check runs in your browser.Fix it automatically when it is one of the usual mistakesPress Repair. It removes comments, adds missing commas and drops trailing ones, turns single and curly quotes into double quotes, quotes bare keys, and replaces True, False, None, NaN, undefined and Infinity with their JSON equivalents, then says what it changed. Validate again to confirm. Repair does not guess at missing brackets or cut-off files; for those the line and column show where to look.Once the text is valid, the JSON formatter indents it or minifies it to one line, and the tree view shows the structure.A byte order mark at position 0A file saved as "UTF-8 with BOM" starts with three invisible bytes. Some parsers reject them with "Unexpected token in JSON at position 0" (the token is the invisible character). Save the file as plain UTF-8 or strip the first character. The validator reads such files, so if it validates and your program does not, the BOM is the likely difference.Still invalid?Write to support@openanydoc.com and paste the error message and the ten characters around the reported line (no personal data).

title: JSON Formatter Alternative: No Save Links, No Upload
desc: How jsonformatter.org and Code Beautify handle pasted JSON, from their own pages, and a JSON formatter and validator that keeps keys and tokens on your device.
h1s: A jsonformatter.org and Code Beautify alternative
headings: A jsonformatter.org and Code Beautify alternative
The JSON tools that keep your data in the browser
Who should stay with those sites
text: HomeGuidesJSON formatter alternativeA jsonformatter.org and Code Beautify alternativeWhat the popular JSON sites say about saving, sharing and loading your data, where they do more, and JSON tools that keep it in your browser.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerjsonformatter.org and Code Beautify are popular free JSON tools with many converters and a way to save JSON as a shareable link. Both state that much of the work happens in your browser, but their saving and URL-loading features involve their servers, and they ask you not to save sensitive data. If you paste API responses, tokens or configuration files, OpenAnyDoc formats, validates and compares JSON in your browser and has no save-online feature at all.What jsonformatter.org says (checked 20 November 2026)From its home page and privacy policy:Validation: "Your JSON Data gets validated in the browser itself." The page also says it keeps the last formatted JSON in the browser's local storage.Saving: you can save JSON online without logging in, and its FAQ says such data "will become public". To keep it private, it asks you to log in. Links can expire after an hour, or after 30 days or never with an account.Sharing and loading: it supports URL linking for sharing JSON and a "Load URL" option for external data.Its privacy policy says, in capitals, "DO NOT SAVE SENSITIVE DATA USING THE SAVE FUNCTIONALITY", and that traffic is measured with Google Analytics and Clicky.Its pages don't say whether formatting or converting ever sends your JSON to a server.What Code Beautify says (checked 20 November 2026)From its JSON viewer page and privacy policy:Processing: its privacy policy says "99% of our tools are doing processing on browser using Java Script" and that it does not store data unless you use the Save Online feature.URLs and files: the same policy says that with URL loading and file upload, data travels between server and client, though it is not stored, and uploaded files are deleted.Saving: the JSON viewer page lets you save JSON as a link and share it. The policy says public data can be indexed by Google, suggests logging in to keep saved data private, and asks you not to save passwords, keys or real production data.Its pages don't say which of its tools are in the 1% that do not run in the browser.Where those sites do moreTo be fair about the choice, both sites offer things OpenAnyDoc does not. Code Beautify converts JSON to Excel, HTML, TSV, text and Base64, and jsonformatter.org adds RSS to JSON and many tools for XML, HTML and CSS. Both let you save JSON as a link to send to a colleague, which OpenAnyDoc cannot do, and both have accounts that keep your saved snippets. For public sample data, that sharing is handy.What OpenAnyDoc does differentlyEvery OpenAnyDoc JSON tool runs in your browser. Pasted JSON and opened files stay in the page's memory until you download a copy, and closing the tab discards them. There is no save-online button, no share link and no account, so nothing can become public by mistake. The site has no analytics.The page's security policy only lets it contact its own site, which you can check yourself in the browser's network panel. There is one exception, and you start it: "Open from a URL" on the JSON pages fetches the https address you type directly from your browser, through a separate frame that is allowed to do only that. The pages work offline once loaded, and JSON files up to 10 MB open.The JSON tools that keep your data in the browserEach of these works on your own device:JSON formatter: pretty print with 1 to 8 spaces or a tab, minify, and sort keys; long integers are kept digit for digit.JSON validator: shows the line and column of an error, and Repair fixes trailing commas, comments, single quotes and unquoted keys.JSON viewer: tree, table and text views, with editing and download.Compare JSON: differences by key and path, ignoring key order.JSON Schema, JSONPath queries, and code types for TypeScript, Python, Go, Java and C#; conversions to CSV, YAML and XML.Mask data: replace emails, names and other personal fields with tokens before you share a file.Side by sideThe main differences, in short:Where JSON is processed: jsonformatter.org validates in the browser, and its pages don't say more; Code Beautify says most tools run in the browser; OpenAnyDoc, every tool in the browser.Save online and share links: both sites, yes (public without login); OpenAnyDoc, no.Loading from a URL: both sites, yes, and Code Beautify says the data passes through its server; OpenAnyDoc, yes, fetched by your browser directly.Analytics: both sites name Google Analytics in their privacy policies; OpenAnyDoc has none.Number of converters: both sites, more.Who should stay with those sitesIf your JSON is public sample data and you want to send a link to it, or you need a converter OpenAnyDoc lacks, jsonformatter.org and Code Beautify do that well. If the JSON holds API keys, tokens, customer records or internal configuration, use a tool that keeps it in your browser, mask the personal fields before sharing, and follow your company's rules on where such data may go.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe what you need (no personal data, and never paste a real token).

desc: Turn a CSV into a Markdown table for a README, docs or AI chat: header and separator lines, column alignment, pipes and line breaks in cells, and wide tables.
h1s: How to make a Markdown table from a CSV file
headings: How to make a Markdown table from a CSV file
What a Markdown table is made of
Pipes, line breaks and other characters in cells
The header row decides the columns
What a Markdown table cannot hold
Pasting the table into a chat
text:
HomeGuidesMarkdown table from CSVHow to make a Markdown table from a CSV fileWhat a Markdown table is made of, how to align its columns, and what to do about pipes, line breaks and wide tables.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerOpen or paste the CSV in CSV to Markdown: the first row becomes the table header, a separator line follows, and every other row becomes one line between pipes. Copy the result into a GitHub README, an issue, your docs or a chat, or download it as an .md file. Pipes inside cells are escaped for you, so the columns stay in place.What a Markdown table is made ofA Markdown table is plain text that GitHub, GitLab and most Markdown editors draw as a table. It has three parts:The header line: the column names between pipes, such as | Item | Qty | Price |.The separator line: three dashes per column, such as | --- | --- | --- |. Without it the lines are shown as ordinary text.One line per row, with the cells in the same order as the header.AlignmentThe converter writes plain --- separators, which most readers show left-aligned. To align a column, edit its part of the separator line after you paste: :--- for left, :---: for centre and ---: for right. Right-aligning number columns makes prices and totals easier to compare. Only the separator line changes; the cells stay as they are. GitHub and GitLab follow these colons; a few simple editors ignore them and show every column the same way.Pipes, line breaks and other characters in cellsBecause the pipe marks a column border, a | inside a cell would split it in two. The converter writes it as \|, which readers show as a plain pipe. A few other cases are worth knowing:A line break inside a cell is written as
. GitHub shows it as a new line within the cell; some editors show the tag as text, so shorten such cells if the table is going elsewhere.Markdown inside cells still works: *text* becomes italic and backticks become code. If a cell holds asterisks or underscores that should stay as they are, check the rendered table.Accented and Arabic letters stay as they are. The delimiter (comma, semicolon, tab or pipe) and the encoding are detected from the file, so a CSV saved by Excel in Europe or an Arabic Windows CSV converts without changes.The header row decides the columnsA Markdown table needs a header, so the first row of the CSV always becomes it. If your file has no header row, add one in the CSV viewer before converting, even if it is only Column 1, Column 2.The header also sets the number of columns. A row with fewer cells gets empty ones at the end; a row with more cells than the header loses the extra ones. Give every column a name and nothing is dropped.Wide and long tablesMarkdown has no limit on columns, but a reader does. On GitHub a wide table scrolls sideways, and on a phone more than five or six columns get hard to follow. If the table is for people to read:Remove the columns readers do not need before converting.If you have few rows and many columns, flip them with Transpose so each field becomes a row.Keep the full data as a CSV file in the repository and show a short table that links to it.What a Markdown table cannot holdThese limits come from Markdown itself, not from the converter, so no tool can get around them:No merged cells and no cells that span rows: complex layouts flatten into simple rows.No colours, fonts or cell borders; style comes from wherever the table is shown.No formulas: the table holds text. Totals must be in the CSV already.No second header row; if your CSV has two, merge them into one line of names first.Long tables in the converterThe preview shows the first 5,000 lines of the table. Copy and Download always take the whole table, so nothing is cut from what you paste. The file is read by your browser and never uploaded, which matters when the CSV is an export from a work system.Pasting the table into a chatChatGPT, Claude and Gemini read Markdown tables well, because each value sits under its column name. A table costs more tokens than the same data as CSV, so for large tables count first with the token counter. If the data comes from a workbook, Excel to Markdown does the same job sheet by sheet, and the guide on giving an AI chat a spreadsheet covers size, formulas and hiding personal data.Step by stepFrom file to rendered table:Open CSV to Markdown and choose the .csv or .tsv file, or paste the CSV text into the box.Check the preview: the header, the separator, then one line per row.Click Copy, paste the table into your README, issue or note, and adjust the separator line if you want alignment.Preview the page (on GitHub, the Preview tab) before you commit or post.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and paste the first two lines of the CSV and where the table goes wrong (no personal data).

title: How to Make a Scanned PDF Searchable With OCR, No Upload
desc: Make a scanned PDF searchable: what OCR does, English and Arabic, why it need not upload your file, how accurate it is, and how to get the text into Word.
h1s: How to make a scanned PDF searchable
headings: How to make a scanned PDF searchable
What OCR changes, and what it does not
Does OCR need to upload your file?
text: HomeGuidesMake a scanned PDF searchableHow to make a scanned PDF searchableWhat text recognition adds to a scan, where it runs, how far to trust it, and what to do with the text afterwards.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerA scanned PDF holds pictures of pages, so there is no text to search or copy. Text recognition (OCR) reads the words in those pictures and lays them over each page as invisible text. OCR PDF does this in your browser, in English, Arabic or both, without uploading the file; the first use loads the text reader from this site, and after that it works offline.Is your PDF a scan?Open the PDF and try to select a word, or press Ctrl+F (Cmd+F on a Mac) and search for a word you can see. If nothing selects and nothing is found, the page is a picture. PDFs made by a scanner, a phone app or Scan to PDF are usually like this, and so are documents that were printed and scanned back.Some PDFs mix both: typed pages with a few scanned ones. OCR PDF leaves pages that already have text as they are, unless you untick Leave pages that already have text.What OCR changes, and what it does notThe scan stays exactly as sharp as it was. OCR adds a layer of invisible text, word by word, over the places where the words appear. The page looks the same, but search finds words, you can select and copy text, and other tools can now read it.It does not make the page editable like a document: the words you see are still the picture. To change the wording, convert the searchable copy to Word, as explained in why you can't edit text in a PDF.Does OCR need to upload your file?Many online OCR services, and cloud apps that turn a PDF into a document, read the file on their own servers, so the scan has to be uploaded. That is a real concern for scanned contracts, bank letters or medical forms.OCR PDF reads the text on your own device. The first time you use it, it loads the text reader and the English and Arabic language data, about 10 MB, from this site itself, not from another company. Your browser keeps them, so later uses start at once and work offline. You can check it in your browser's network panel: the reader loads the first time, and the PDF is never sent anywhere.English, Arabic or bothChoose the language of the text before you start: English, Arabic, or Arabic and English for pages that mix them, such as a bilingual form. These are the only languages it reads. If it finds no words, check the language choice first, then try a sharper scan.How accurate it isRecognition is good on clean printed text and gets worse as the scan does. Know its limits before you rely on the result:Blurry, small or faint text gives more mistakes; check names, numbers and amounts that matter.Handwriting is not read reliably and usually comes out wrong.Tables and columns are read as lines of words, not as a table.Slightly tilted scans are fine, because words follow their line's slope; a page photographed at a steep angle is better straightened first with Scan to PDF.Reading takes a few seconds a page, depending on your device.Make it searchableOpen OCR PDF, choose the scanned PDF, pick the language and click Make searchable. Each page is read in turn. Download the copy and search it in any PDF reader, including the PDF viewer here.Then get the text outOnce the PDF has a text layer, the conversion tools can read it:PDF to text saves every page's words as a plain .txt file, Arabic in reading order.PDF to Word rebuilds paragraphs, headings and lists in an editable document.Translate PDF turns English into Arabic or Arabic into English, and also needs OCR first for a scan.If Arabic copied from a PDF comes out reversed, see fixing Arabic text copied from a PDF.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe the scan you are trying to read (no personal data).

title: How to Open a CSV File Without Excel: Free Ways, No Upload
desc: Open a CSV without Excel for free: in your browser with no upload, Google Sheets, LibreOffice, Numbers or a text editor, plus fixes for big files and Arabic.
h1s: How to open a CSV file without Excel
headings: How to open a CSV file without Excel
In your browser, with nothing uploaded
The file opens in one column
What a CSV can and cannot hold
Need an Excel file after all?
text: HomeGuidesOpen CSV without ExcelHow to open a CSV file without ExcelThe free options, which of them upload your file, and what to do when a CSV is too big, lands in one column or shows broken Arabic.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerA CSV file is plain text: one row per line, with the values separated by commas. Excel is only one of many programs that read it. A browser-based viewer, Google Sheets, LibreOffice Calc, Apple Numbers and even a text editor all open it for free. They differ in three ways: whether the file is uploaded, how large a file they handle, and whether they get the separator and the encoding right.In your browser, with nothing uploadedDrop the file on the CSV viewer. It finds the separator (comma, semicolon, tab or pipe) and the encoding for you, and shows the rows as a table you can sort, filter, search and edit, with undo and redo. You can run SQL queries on the table, draw a chart of the rows shown, and download the file again as CSV, or as an Excel workbook when someone needs one. Your browser reads the file itself, so customer lists and exports never leave your computer, and leading zeros and long numbers stay as they were written.Free spreadsheet appsEach of these opens a CSV as a sheet:LibreOffice Calc (Windows, Mac and Linux) shows an import window first, where you choose the character set and the separator before the data loads. That window is why it rarely gets Arabic text or semicolons wrong.Apple Numbers (Mac, iPhone and iPad) opens a CSV directly and can export it as an Excel file.Google Sheets opens a CSV after you upload it to Google Drive or bring it in with File, Import. It needs an account and keeps the file on Google's servers, which is fine for most files but not for payroll or customer data.In a text editorNotepad, TextEdit or any code editor shows the raw file: each line is a row and the commas are visible. It is the quickest way to see which separator the file uses, whether the first line holds the headers, and whether values are wrapped in quotes. A wide table is hard to read this way, and deleting a single comma shifts every value after it into the wrong column, so edit with care.On a phoneMobile browsers open the CSV viewer the same way: tap Choose a file and pick the CSV from Files or your downloads. On an iPhone or iPad, Numbers opens it as a spreadsheet, and on Android the Google Sheets app opens it with your Google account.Files too big for ExcelAn Excel sheet stops at 1,048,576 rows, and a file of a few hundred megabytes can freeze it long before that. The large CSV viewer has no row limit of its own: a 120,000-row file opens in under a second, and the real limit is your device's memory, with a warning above 50 MB. Why Excel cuts the file short, and other ways around it, are explained in CSV too big for Excel.The file opens in one columnIf every row lands in column A, the file uses a separator your program does not expect: commas where your region uses semicolons, or the other way round. A viewer that detects the separator, LibreOffice's import window and Excel's own import from text all solve it; CSV opens in one column explains each fix. To rewrite the file with the separator you need, use Change CSV delimiter.Arabic text turns into symbolsWhen Arabic shows as "Ø§Ù„" or question marks, the program read a UTF-8 file with the wrong encoding. The CSV viewer reads UTF-8, UTF-16 and older Windows-1256 files correctly and shows Arabic right to left. For Excel itself, the guide to broken Arabic in a CSV shows how to make a copy that opens correctly with a double-click.What a CSV can and cannot holdA CSV holds only values: no formulas, colours, column widths or second sheets. Anything you format in a spreadsheet app is lost when you save it as CSV again, so keep a workbook when you need those, and use the CSV to pass data between programs. The first line usually holds the column names, and a value that contains the separator or a line break is wrapped in double quotes.Need an Excel file after all?If a colleague or a system asks for an .xlsx, CSV to Excel turns the file into a workbook in your browser, with a bold header row, real numbers, and values like 007 or long IDs kept as text so no digit is lost. You never need Excel installed to make it, and the CSV is not uploaded.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe the file (no personal data).

title: How to Open a DOCX File Without Word: Free Options
desc: Free ways to open a .docx file without Microsoft Word: in your browser with no upload, LibreOffice, Google Docs, Apple Pages or a phone, and what each keeps.
h1s: How to open a DOCX file without Word
headings: How to open a DOCX file without Word
In your browser, with nothing uploaded
Need to change the file, not just open it?
text: HomeGuidesOpen DOCX without WordHow to open a DOCX file without WordThe free options, which of them upload your document, and how much of its layout and formatting each one keeps.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 2, 2026 · Updated November 23, 2026The short answerA .docx file is a Word document, but you do not need Microsoft Word to open it. A browser-based viewer, LibreOffice Writer, Google Docs and Apple Pages all read it for free. They differ in two ways: whether the file is uploaded, and how much of the layout and formatting they keep.In your browser, with nothing uploadedDrop the file on the Word viewer. The document opens as pages with its page size and margins, fonts, tables, pictures, lists, headers and footers with page numbers, and Arabic paragraphs and tables run right to left. You can zoom in, fit the page to your screen and download the original file again. The viewer shows documents without editing them; the browser tools further down change them. Password-protected documents cannot be opened.Save it as a PDFTo send or print the document, open it in the Word viewer and click Print / Save as PDF, or use Word to PDF to get a PDF with searchable text in one step. With Print / Save as PDF, your browser's print dialog opens with only the document's pages; choose Save as PDF (Microsoft Print to PDF on Windows) as the printer. Either way the PDF is made on your computer, so the document is not uploaded for this either.Need to change the file, not just open it?These tools change a Word document in your browser, without uploading it:Word to PDF saves the document as a PDF, page by page, with text you can still select and search.Find and replace in Word replaces a word or phrase everywhere, headers and footnotes included, and keeps its formatting.Merge Word (in beta) joins two or more documents into one .docx, each starting on a new page.Remove Word comments deletes the comments and accepts or rejects every tracked change, for a clean copy to send.Word metadata shows who wrote, edited and saved the document, and removes those details in one click.Free desktop appsThese work offline and keep the file on your computer:LibreOffice Writer (Windows, Mac and Linux) opens, edits and saves .docx and keeps most formatting. It is the closest free equivalent to desktop Word.Apple Pages (Mac, iPhone and iPad) opens .docx and can export back to the Word format; some Word-only features are converted or dropped.On a Mac, selecting the file in Finder and pressing the Space bar shows a quick preview, and TextEdit opens it with simpler formatting.Online suites (the file is uploaded)Google Docs opens a .docx after you upload it to Google Drive, and Word for the web does the same with OneDrive. Both need an account, and the document is stored on their servers. That is fine for most files, but not for contracts, HR letters or anything you are not allowed to share. If you are unsure whether a site uploads your file, you can check it yourself.On a phoneMobile browsers open OpenAnyDoc the same way: tap Choose a file and pick the document from Files or your downloads; the page fits the screen width. Microsoft's Word app and Google Docs also have phone apps; both work with your account.Older and related formatsA few other extensions turn up next to .docx:.doc is the Word 97 to 2003 format. OpenAnyDoc does not open it; LibreOffice, Pages and Word do, and can save it as .docx, which then opens here..docm is a document with macros and .dotx a template. The Word viewer opens both; the macros never run outside Word..odt is the OpenDocument text format that LibreOffice saves by default, and .rtf an older rich text format. Word, LibreOffice and Pages open both, and the Word viewer here opens .odt too.What may look differentOnly Word draws everything exactly. Other apps, OpenAnyDoc included, replace fonts that are not installed on your device with similar ones, so lines and pages can break in other places, and charts, text boxes and some drawing shapes may be simplified. If the exact layout matters, keep the original file or ask the sender for a PDF.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe the document (no personal data).

title: Open HEIC Photos on Windows Without Installing Anything
desc: Why Windows won't open iPhone HEIC photos, how to view or convert them to JPG in your browser with nothing to install, and how to make the iPhone shoot JPG.
h1s: How to open iPhone HEIC photos on Windows
headings: How to open iPhone HEIC photos on Windows
Why Windows may not open it
Open it in your browser, with nothing installed
What to expect from the JPG
Stop the iPhone making HEIC files
text: HomeGuidesOpen HEIC on WindowsHow to open iPhone HEIC photos on WindowsWhat a HEIC file is, why Windows needs an add-on for it, and how to open or convert one in any browser without uploading it.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerWindows opens iPhone HEIC photos in its Photos app once the HEIF Image Extensions from the Microsoft Store are installed. If you can't or don't want to install anything, open the photo in your browser with OpenAnyDoc's Image viewer, or turn it into a JPG with HEIC to JPG; both work in Chrome, Edge and Firefox on Windows, and the photo stays on your PC. To avoid the problem next time, set the iPhone to save photos as JPG.What a HEIC file isHEIC is the file type iPhones use for photos by default. It is a photo saved in the HEIF format, which takes less space than a JPG at a similar quality, so the same phone storage holds more photos. A Mac opens it in Photos and Preview with nothing to install, an iPhone or iPad opens it in Photos, and most Android phones open it in Google Photos or their own gallery app.The file may end in .heic or .heif. Both are the same kind of photo, and both open with the steps below. Some Android phones save HEIC photos too.Why Windows may not open itWindows reads HEIC through an add-on rather than out of the box. The usual one is the HEIF Image Extensions, a free download from the Microsoft Store; once it is installed, the Photos app opens HEIC photos. On some PCs the photos open only when the HEVC Video Extensions are installed as well, because the picture inside a HEIC file is compressed the same way as HEVC video; those are sold in the Store, and some PCs come with them.That route is fine on your own PC. It does not help on a work or school computer where the Store is blocked, on a shared or borrowed PC, or when you only need to open one photo once. Browsers can't help on their own either: Chrome, Edge and Firefox don't show HEIC themselves, which is also why many websites refuse it as an upload.Open it in your browser, with nothing installedOpenAnyDoc reads the photo on your PC. The first time you open a HEIC file in Chrome, Edge or Firefox, a HEIC decoder loads from this site and your browser keeps it; the photo itself is never uploaded.To look at a photo: open the Image viewer and drop the .heic file on the page. You can zoom, fit it to the window and see the camera, the date taken and, if the photo has one, its GPS location.To use it somewhere else: open HEIC to JPG, add one photo or a whole folder, choose the quality (90 keeps them looking the same) and download a JPG, or a ZIP of all of them.From the viewer, the next steps can compress, resize or clean the photo, or turn it into a PDF, without choosing the file again.What to expect from the JPGThe JPG comes out upright and at full size. It is usually larger than the HEIC it came from; if it is too big for an email or a form, see how to reduce a photo's file size. A few other points:A few HEIC photos taken with the newest iPhone settings may not decode. Save those as JPG on the phone first, with the setting in the next section.Live Photos become a still JPG; the short video is not kept.The camera, date and GPS details are not copied into the JPG. That is good for sharing, but keep the original if you want the date taken in your albums.Stop the iPhone making HEIC filesTwo iPhone settings help. They change the photos you take or copy from now on, not the ones already saved.Settings, Camera, Formats, Most Compatible: the camera saves new photos as JPG instead of HEIC. They take more space on the phone.Settings, Photos, Transfer to Mac or PC, Automatic: photos copied to a computer with a cable are converted to a compatible format on the way.Before you share the photoA photo can show more than you mean to share: the faces in it and, inside the file, where it was taken. Before you post a converted photo you can blur faces in it, and the guide to removing the location from a photo explains what the file carries. Every step runs in your browser; to be sure, check for yourself that no file is uploaded.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com if a HEIC photo will not open, and say which phone took it and which browser you used (no personal data, and please don't attach the photo).

title: How to Open a JSON File: Browser, Phone, Editor, Online
desc: How to open a JSON file on Windows, Mac or a phone: in your browser, a text or code editor, or a free online viewer, and what to do when the file will not open.
h1s: How to open a JSON file
headings: How to open a JSON file
The quickest way: open it in your browser
On Windows or a Mac with no extra software
If the file will not open
text: HomeGuidesHow to open a JSON fileHow to open a JSON fileEvery way to open and read a .json file, from the quickest to the most powerful, and how to fix one that will not open.By OpenAnyDoc · Published October 30, 2026 · Updated November 23, 2026What a JSON file isJSON (JavaScript Object Notation) is plain text that stores data as objects of "key": value pairs and as lists in square brackets. APIs, configuration files and data exports use it. Any program that opens text can open a .json file; the hard part is reading it when it is one long line or nested many levels deep.The quickest way: open it in your browserDrop the file on the JSON viewer, or paste JSON with Ctrl+V (Cmd+V on a Mac). It shows a tree you can fold, a table when the file is a list of objects, and the text with line numbers. Nothing is uploaded, and it works on a phone too: tap Choose a file and pick the .json from Files or your downloads. Files up to 10 MB open.On Windows or a Mac with no extra softwareEvery browser opens JSON: drag the file onto a Chrome, Edge or Firefox window. Firefox shows a built-in viewer with a collapsible tree; the others show the text. Notepad on Windows and TextEdit on a Mac open it as text too: right-click the file, choose Open with, and pick the editor. They are fine for small files, but long lines and deep nesting are hard to follow.In a code editorIf you work with JSON often, a code editor such as the free Visual Studio Code colours the syntax, folds objects and marks errors. Format Document (Shift+Alt+F on Windows, Shift+Option+F on a Mac) indents a file saved on one line.Make a one-line file readableA file saved on a single line is valid but unreadable. The JSON formatter indents it with 2 or 4 spaces (anything from 1 to 8, or a tab), can sort the keys, and minifies it again when you need a small file.If the file will not openThe message usually says why:"Unexpected token" or "Unexpected end of JSON input" means the text breaks a JSON rule: a trailing comma, single quotes or a comment. The JSON validator shows the line and column and repairs the common mistakes, and the guide to unexpected token errors explains each message.A file that starts with < is an HTML page saved with a .json name, often an error page from a server.A file with one JSON object per line (.jsonl or .ndjson) is JSON Lines: each line is a separate document, so an ordinary JSON parser rejects the file as a whole. The JSON viewer opens .jsonl and .ndjson files line by line.Above 10 MB OpenAnyDoc refuses the file to keep the page responsive; a code editor or a command-line tool such as jq handles larger ones.Turn JSON into a spreadsheetIf the file is a list of records, the JSON to CSV converter flattens it into columns (nested fields become headers such as address.city) and opens the result as a table you can download and open in Excel.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and say what you see when you open the file (no personal data).

title: How to Open a PDF Without Adobe: Free Ways on Any Device
desc: Open a PDF without Adobe Reader: any browser, Preview on Mac, Files on iPhone, Drive on Android, why a PDF will not open, and how to fill and sign it for free.
h1s: How to open a PDF without Adobe
headings: How to open a PDF without Adobe
In your browser here, with nothing uploaded
Fill in and sign a PDF without Adobe
Choose which app opens your PDFs
Do you need Acrobat at all?
text: HomeGuidesOpen PDF without AdobeHow to open a PDF without AdobeThe free programs every computer and phone already has, why a PDF sometimes will not open, and how to fill in and sign one without Adobe.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026The short answerYou do not need Adobe Acrobat or Adobe Reader to open a PDF. Every modern web browser, including Chrome, Edge, Firefox and Safari, opens one: drag the file onto a window. A Mac opens PDFs in Preview, an iPhone or iPad in the Files or Books app, and an Android phone in the Google Drive app that most of them come with. All of these are free and usually already installed.On a computerWhat each system already has:Windows: PDFs open in Microsoft Edge by default. It zooms, searches, highlights and fills in forms.Mac: Preview opens PDFs, fills in forms, adds text and signatures, and reorders pages.Linux: the document viewer that comes with most desktops opens PDFs.Any system: Chrome, Firefox and Safari show a PDF in a tab. Drag the file onto the window, or press Ctrl+O (Cmd+O on a Mac) and choose it.In your browser here, with nothing uploadedDrop the file on the PDF viewer. It shows every page in one scroll with thumbnails, a page counter, zoom from 50% to 400%, fit to width and rotation, and searches the text with highlighted matches, Arabic included, in reading order. A password-protected PDF asks for its password, which is used only in that tab. The viewer looks the same on every device and keeps working offline once the page has loaded, and the file is read by your own browser, so it is never uploaded.On a phoneOn an iPhone or iPad, tap the PDF in the Files app to read it; the Markup button adds text and a signature, and the Books app keeps PDFs in a library. On Android, the Google Drive app opens PDFs from your downloads or email. The PDF viewer here works in a phone browser too, with the page thumbnails opening from the toolbar.Why won't my PDF open?Most PDFs that refuse to open, or open wrongly, have one of these problems:It asks for a password. The file is encrypted: type the password in your viewer. If you know the password and want a copy without it, Unlock PDF removes it on your device. It does not guess or crack passwords, so use it only for files you are allowed to unlock.It is damaged. A download that stopped early, a broken email attachment or a faulty export leaves a file that viewers call damaged. Repair PDF rebuilds the file's index and saves the pages that are intact; a page that is missing from the file cannot be brought back.It opens, but you cannot select or search the text. The PDF is a scan, so each page is a picture. OCR PDF reads the words in English or Arabic and gives you a PDF you can search, select and copy.It is not really a PDF. A file that was renamed to .pdf, or one of only a few bytes, opens in no PDF viewer; download it again or ask the sender for a new copy.Fill in and sign a PDF without AdobeChrome, Edge and Firefox let you type into the fields of most fillable forms, and Preview does on a Mac. To fill in a form and save a clean copy without uploading it, use Fill PDF form: it handles text fields, multi-line boxes, checkboxes, radio buttons and drop-down lists, in English or Arabic, and can flatten the answers onto the page. XFA forms, an older Adobe format, are not supported there and usually need Adobe Reader.For a signature, the guide to signing a PDF without Adobe walks through the free options on a computer and on a phone, and when a picture of a signature is not enough.Choose which app opens your PDFsIf PDFs keep opening in a program you do not want, change the default. On Windows, right-click a PDF, choose Open with, then Choose another app, pick the one you want and choose to always use it. On a Mac, select a PDF in Finder, choose File, Get Info, pick the app under Open with and click Change All. On a phone, the share or open menu lets you pick the app each time.Do you need Acrobat at all?Adobe Acrobat Reader is free as well, and Adobe's paid Acrobat adds features such as editing a PDF's original text. You need neither to read, print, search, fill in or sign a PDF, or to merge, split, rotate and number its pages: browsers and the free PDF tools here do that on your own device.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe what happens when you open the file (no personal data).

desc: Free ways to open a .pptx file without PowerPoint: in your browser with no upload, Google Slides, LibreOffice Impress, Keynote or a phone, and old .ppt files.
h1s: How to open a PPTX file without PowerPoint
headings: How to open a PPTX file without PowerPoint
In your browser, with nothing uploaded
Need the words, not the slides?
Need to change the file, not just open it?
text: HomeGuidesOpen PPTX without PowerPointHow to open a PPTX file without PowerPointThe free options, which of them upload your presentation, which of them edit it, and what to do with an old .ppt file.By OpenAnyDoc · Published November 20, 2026 · Updated November 23, 2026The short answerA .pptx file is a PowerPoint presentation, but you do not need PowerPoint to open it. A browser-based viewer, Google Slides, LibreOffice Impress and Apple Keynote all open it for free. Microsoft's standalone PowerPoint Viewer has been retired, so these are the options today. They differ in whether the file is uploaded, whether you can edit it, and how faithfully they draw the slides.In your browser, with nothing uploadedDrop the file on the PowerPoint viewer. It is in beta and shows presentations; it does not edit them. What it does:Shows the slides with their text, fonts, pictures, tables, shapes and backgrounds, and moves between them with thumbnails, the previous and next buttons or the arrow keys.Shows the speaker notes under the slide, and a grid of all slides to jump to any of them.Presents full screen, or in a presenter view with the current and next slide, your notes and a timer while the audience sees the slide in a second window.Searches the slide text and notes, prints one slide per page, and saves the slides as a PDF or as PNG pictures.Does not play animations or transitions, and simplifies some effects and charts.Free apps that also editIf you need to change the slides, these open and save .pptx:LibreOffice Impress (Windows, Mac and Linux) opens, edits and saves .pptx, and opens old .ppt files too.Apple Keynote (Mac, iPhone and iPad) opens .pptx and can export back to PowerPoint; some effects and fonts are replaced.Google Slides opens a .pptx after you upload it to Google Drive, and PowerPoint for the web does the same with OneDrive. Both need an account and store the presentation on their servers, which is fine for most decks but not for unreleased plans or figures.On a phoneMobile browsers open the PowerPoint viewer the same way: tap Choose a file and pick the presentation; the slide fills the width of the screen and the buttons move between slides. On an iPhone or iPad, the Files app shows a quick preview and Keynote opens the file. Microsoft's PowerPoint app and Google Slides also have phone apps; both work with your account.Old .ppt files and related formatsThe .ppt extension is the PowerPoint 97 to 2003 format, a different kind of file. OpenAnyDoc's viewer does not open it. Open it in LibreOffice Impress or PowerPoint and save it as .pptx, and the new file opens here. These related extensions do open in the viewer:.ppsx is a slide show: the same content as a .pptx, set to start presenting when opened in PowerPoint..potx is a template that new presentations are made from..pptm is a presentation with macros. The slides open; the macros are never run.Need the words, not the slides?To quote a deck in a report, search it or paste it into an AI chat, turn it into text. PowerPoint to Markdown writes each slide's title and bullet points, with the speaker notes under them, as a clean outline; pictures, charts and the layout are left out. The viewer itself can also export an outline of titles, text and notes as Markdown or plain text.Need to change the file, not just open it?The viewer does not edit slides, but these tools work on a whole presentation in your browser, without uploading it:PowerPoint to PDF saves the presentation as a PDF, one page per slide, with text you can still select and search.Merge PowerPoint (in beta) joins two or more presentations into one .pptx file, in the order you choose.Split PowerPoint cuts a presentation into several .pptx files, one per slide or by the slide ranges you type.Search PowerPoint finds a word in every slide and speaker note, with the slide number of each match.Watermark PowerPoint puts a text watermark such as CONFIDENTIAL or DRAFT on every slide.Which option to chooseA simple rule of thumb:You only need to read or present the slides, and the deck is confidential: a browser viewer that does not upload it.You need to change the slides: LibreOffice Impress or Keynote, on your own computer.You are working on the deck with other people: Google Slides or PowerPoint for the web, if the content may be stored there.You only need the words: PowerPoint to Markdown.What may look differentOnly PowerPoint draws everything exactly. Other apps, OpenAnyDoc included, replace fonts that are not installed on your device with similar ones, so text can wrap differently. In the viewer here, SmartArt shows as PowerPoint last drew it, charts are approximate, embedded video may not play, and a slide it cannot draw yet shows a note instead of a broken layout, while the other slides are not affected. If the exact look matters, ask the sender for a PDF, which every browser opens.Questions?Write to support@openanydoc.com and describe the presentation (no personal data).
